body:
Moving to a relay chain without evm is a new idea and the most important part for edgeware is to get an upgraded runtime.


The main focus should be on getting edgeware's Runtime upgraded, switching to native vanilla substrate, getting the ethereum types and the latest ethereum types implemented, expanding the transaction functionality to extend it with ethereum smart contract execution and format updates, with other words getting erup-5 to work, which will end with a similar chain as moonbeam but there is still a lot of differences.    



 After going over this more on a techincal level, and after breaking the grandpa crate(which is due to some weird bug somewhere in the code), as well as talking with Remz about this.    


The best way to go forward in order to get an updated runtime and not break mayor functionality is to get erup-5 to work, how will this be done? Me and Remz will go through the code and reapply the ethereum upgrades. This has taken way more time and resources then expected but we are solving it!

Edgeware as a "**Grassroots relay chain**" with an incubation model, spawning chains from early stage and capturing value through a stake of each chain,  similar to an accelerator, is both a complimentary model to the subverse, and it also arguably a truly value proposition that will attract a lot of smart funds. 


**How can we capture value from chains properly?**
We can create contractual relationships with the founding teams and the chains. 

**What if the incubated chain wants to move to Polkadot?**
That is fine we can have as a clause that they must implement a snapshot like with Kabocha. 

The above also leads us to creating novel new legal strcutures which are both digital and physical. We have none other than the most valuable person who understands law in our commmunity (Mr Miyagi of Law), [ Frank O'Collins.](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/discussion/4978-law-decoded-seminars-and-delawareuk-dao-pilots)

From what we've captured from conversations with Rich, Remz and Shankar is no one has disagreed with becoming a relay chain that spawns its own chains. 

The question is whether to switch evm off or try and keep it alive until deciding with to spawn an EdgEVM parachain? Some may believe including myself not have an EDGEVM parachain at all, if we are to be principled about this. 

It would be great if we can be a relay with no evm. Thus it makes us create a computer with different purpose fibers. 

Btw Polkadot got the idea for heterogenous multichain network from the [Chain Fibers (2014) article](https://ethereum.github.io/blog/2015/04/05/blockchain-scalability-chain-fibers-redux/) by Gavin. He could already see the problems that would face an evm global machine. 

Relay is a principled design and a clear vision. Mixing it with evm smart contracts is unnecessary and convoluted.

One final point on this related to the idea of creating an EVM parachain off Edgeware relay...

> The question is whether to switch evm off or try and keep it alive until deciding with to spawn an EdgEVM parachain? Some may believe including myself not have an EDGEVM parachain at all, if we are to be principled about this. 

To be consistent, we could support an EVM chain that had a clear focus as an 'appchain'.

But not an EVM chain that had Dapps, but something very specific, that could only be achieved with this approach.

Moonbeam/river is an EVM swiss-army knife, there is no need for another. 

The key question for those wanting EVM, is why and what for?

Is there a clear proposition, application or community that we would build this for?

If we are incubating grass-roots chains, then this EVM parachain is one of those. 

If it has no purpose, other than being a generic EVM parachain, then it destroys our own narrative before we've even begun.

We are now sliding towards discussing whether we want smart contracts or not, which is a slightly different topic than what I was focusing on.
My point was purely about the proposal which is about having smart contracts, but making them a parachain, and the concerns I have about that plan, no more.

About smart contracts vs dedicated-chains specifically: I also like the app-chain concept, not because I think it's necessarily "better" in the absolute (I had tried to point out how this is just a different set of tradeoffs), but because it fits much more naturally within the substrate ecosystem. 
However, my point earlier is that the appchain concept makes sense mostly for specialized use-cases that aim at being compute-efficient and cheaper than having all at base layer. And smart contracts are generalized platforms that could host many heterogenous cases on the opposite. So:

1/ If we are to get smart contracts, that probably shouldn't be hosted in a parachain.
2/ If we do not want smart contracts, we don't need a smart contract parachain either.
3/ Whether we have contracts or not doesn't prevent Edgeware to be a base layer that hosts in-house **specialized** chains.

> it fits much more naturally within the substrate ecosystem
It's true. And this is a very strong reason to do so. Else Edgeware should be a sort of shard or utility of ethereum, like matic polygon,  which it isnt. Edgeware is quite distant form the Ethereum ecosystem currently, at least from where i am standing. 

> 3/ Whether we have contracts or not doesn't prevent Edgeware to be a base layer that hosts in-house **specialized** chains.
Indeed, however its important that the relay does not also contain evm. We dont want to mix conflicting design principles. If we do have evm, it must be on a parachain. Else we are still a smart contract blockchain (with a relay attached).  Also if you look at polkadot's approach, their aim is to simplify the relay by even removing balances and assumingly governance from the relay, so that the relay does only one job.

Why not becoming a relay chain? Formally Edgeware validators ecosystem is several orders of magnitude less safe than Kusama, or Polkadot. So it would be a challenge for any **external** app chain to project deploying there long term. The matter here is a bit different because we are talking in-house incubated chains. But people have to bear in mind that - at the moment - those in-house chains would be the only viable candidates for a relay.

That being set: there are efficiency costs in deploying specific appchains with shared security because of the coupling it involves. I think the agency has some study on this already. 
But even in terms of interoperability/composability, this is a step back: a wasm chain and an EVM chain would not be able to interoperate within the same block. The protocols for direct efficient interactions are still being designed and will require more resources to achieve less efficient interactions than being all at core. Specialized appchains have the advantage of being more gas/compute efficient. That's a tradeoff, but a smart contract (understand "generic") appchain sounds like the worst of both worlds: all the drawbacks of not being at base, but nothing to be gained from specialization.

Last, there is moonbeam which I personally think is an awesome project, but struggles to find much usecase as a polkadot chain. There's moonriver on Kusama, whose target is therefore not well-defined, and there are many more, plasm, whatever... dozens of them. What's proposed is basically a third moonbeam-like on Edgeware (which would not be a very good relay as mentioned). I think it ends up just looking like a (very) poor man's version of the above unfortunately.

The original issue as I understand it is some impossibility to migrate the EVM forward. The solution proposed (launching an EVM parachain on Edgeware) would force to abandon the onchain EVM state totally or migrate it somehow (e.g. re-deploy contracts, and fork the balances). I may sound scary

The original issue as I understand it is some impossibility to migrate the EVM forward. The solution proposed (launching an EVM parachain on Edgeware) would force to abandon the onchain EVM state totally or migrate it somehow (e.g. re-deploy contracts, and fork the balances). I may sound scary, but if there is really a bottleneck for upgrading, I think it's totally acceptable to conduct such as state-breaking move.
However, if we agree that's the cost to pay, why not simply discarding the state and upgrade within the core layer, why doing it within this relay/parachain framework? 
Breaking the state is the proposed solution. Deploying all as a parachain is an idea, but seems totally independent and not part of the solution. We can discuss it but let's not mix it with changes or plans that are probably mandatory on their own.

body:
> So it would be a challenge for any **external** app chain to project deploying there long term.
Totally agree, we fund and create our own parachains. Not bring in "external" projects. After we have a clearer relay path our value will increase, and maybe the market will reflect that. 


> why doing it within this relay/parachain framework?
because multichain is a better design and long term bet. It would be better we chose multichain and ditched evm altogether. It's a clash of philosophies. Having evm on a parachain at least contains it, and satisfies the Edgeware story, best of both worlds. 

> I think it ends up just looking like a (very) poor man's version of the above unfortunately.
It could be argued that Edgeware is already a poor mans version.

It would be better we were the 3rd (grassroots) relay chain in the ecosystem than a smart contract lonely solo chain, which has no real principled design. Smart contracts are a sub-optimal way to build things. That's why many like the multichain minimalist approach to polkadot and their multichain heterogenous implementation.  

> there are efficiency costs in deploying specific appchains with shared security because of the coupling it involves
I can't imagine 1 or 3 parachains would make a huge impact on security. I would be interested to see the analysis made of course.

body:
Let's also really focus on the elephant in the room - Edgeware needs to have a clear, easy to understand and articulate value capture proposition.

Without that we create no demand from investors, since there is not a primary value capture proposition, just a mish-mash of wishful thinking that EVM = magical money ladder to the moon. 

We're evolving towards that, from the technically and economically nebulous "Edgeware is an incubator" which was initially established at launch. 

Having considered this a lot, and with Kabocha close to becoming a KSM parachain and requiring its own consistent narrative and proposition we have two options, all else rn just don't feel tight, focused or credible.

1. **Edgeware remains a solo-chain and continues to fund R&D projects.  **
2. Its primary value capture is in building stake in KAB, which in turn has a clear value capture proposition of taking Edgeware funded R&D and turning it into commercial pilots, retaining a share of future rights and associated revenues. 
3. Those commercial pilots are developed as parachains, that can then onboard to Kusama, and then when they mature Polkadot. 
4. In this model we do not require our own relay and Edgeware retains its own unique status. 
5. It is the simplest approach from where we are.
6. Edgeware only recoups if Kabocha advances the R&D, Kabocha only succeeds, if Edgeware produces great R&D. 
7. The two are clearly long term aligned and this continues the credible narrative that Edgeware is an ashram for curious, committed and inventive people and their ideas.

This is the **primary debate**. 

So does EDG remain a solo-chain? 

or does EDG become a relay chain?

The EVM question needs to be settled after this, conflating them confuses things unnecessarily. 

Once the choice is made, the implementation / structure of where the EVM sits can be made. 

Let's separate out and debate things on their own merits in an iterative, first principles way.

body:
I cannot reply to Rich directly. 
We had the question in the proposals channels, and there is a third option, which is actually following what the original goal of Edgeware was, which is that Edgeware becomes a polkadot parachain.

So does EDG remain a solo-chain?
or does EDG become a relay chain?
or does EDG become a Polkadot parachain
I think this has been understood over my time being around Edgeware for 15 months that EDG main chain will never be a polkadot parachain because it will lose its 12m blocks. There are many prior discussions related to this as that has been the main topic "EDG on DOT or not?". So the answer seems to be "both".

So EDG will most likely remain a solo chain, though there is nothing stop EDG spawning a DOT parachain - like it did for Kabocha on KSM - in the future. 

All we need to know now is we are not closing the possibility of creating a DOT parachain by becoming a relay. 

We we will probably fund multiple DOT and KSM parachains over time. 

Rich highlighted value capture, and Remz says that being a relay makes sense because it suits the substrate ecosystem. 

We have spoken on the Edgeware proposals channel, which i can paste into a comment below. 

But to summarise. Chain spawning makes sense for us to be a grassrots relay, so then we can fund and spawn parachains, capturing share of each of the chains we create, and home them in our relay network. It's clear and decent proposition. If these chain sub-communities want to then connect to different networks then they can, capturing the value in the process.

body: I think this is a good solution, the big thing that has been keeping the ethereum upgrades behind is the expansion of the transaction pool, because the latest ethereum implementations supports several formats of transactions, making them compatible with substrate native ish transaction format. Right now the new formats have been added but it's breaking with .18 polkadot releases: [https://github.com/edgeware-network/edgeware-node/runs/6690462025?check[_suite_focus=true](https://github.com/edgeware-network/edgeware-node/runs/6690462025?check_suite_focus=true)](https://github.com/edgeware-network/edgeware-node/runs/6690462025?check)
